Patch Set 19:

With patch set 19 I moved internal helper methods into .cpp from .hpp, keeping only the API parts in the header, and also split the pinPolarity field into two dbus properties originating from the same bit.

I also simplified the mrBits() function, got rid of hard to understand floating masks and now use much more clear bit counts (widths) and positions.

The combinedWattage field got renamed to combinedVoltages to better reflect its nature. It's just the first byte of a 3-byte Combined Wattage field, and the name combinedWattage was misleading. Also added parsing for combined voltages so that dbus properties will now contain combined voltages in millivolts, not IPMI-encoded voltage indices.

Addressed Tom's comments regarding typos and documentation (at least I hope that documentation is good enough now).

Overall, I hope the code became better and is finally ready for a merge along with the interface definition in https://gerrit.openbmc-project.xyz/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/20588 patch set 2.

Alexander + Yadro etc, I took another look. I noticed the following:

- I'm not wild about the "cool trick" to get the count of types by sticking an unlabeled enum at the end of IpmiMultirecordType, but I can follow it, so fine.
- The fact that this is ugly is kind of a "design feature" of enum class. This is a hacky way to do a lookup table with enums, and the language is telling you so.
- This lookup table only has two out of 10 values implemented, and doesn't give any built in indication that an "unimplemented" value has been accessed.

So, here's my opinion (nothing more, nothing less):
Keep the enum class and listen to what it's telling you. This weird lookup table is not the right way of doing things. Use a helper function, and use the helper function to warn or error when an unimplemented type is called.  It may seem redundant to do a switch on the enum type and assign a value, but it will be easier to understand and maintain than this kind of lookup, and you will be able to make it more featureful (ie support returning an error, warning, exception, whatever you want).

FWIW, I know lots of folks are using auto-formatting in their editors (me included) - so explicitly turning off clang-format is better than hushing the clang presubmit check, because it will become pretty difficult for someone to modify the code _without_ reformatting it later.
